product_hero_content.product_hero_content_title: What is the Greece Golden Visa?

product_hero_content_text.product_hero_content_text_item: The Greece Golden Visa is a residence permit program established by the Greek government.
It is open to non-EU investors and their families through an investment in Greek real estate.
Three generations of your family can live in Greece and travel across the 29 Schengen countries.

product_hero_content_text_subs.product_hero_content_text_sub_item: The €250,000 threshold applies to properties converted from commercial to residential use; taxes and fees are not included.

product_benefits_item_bullets.product_benefits_item_bullet_text: Live, invest in a business, and study in Greece.

product_benefits_items.product_benefits_item_title: Visa-free travel in the Schengen Area

product_benefits_item_bullets.product_benefits_item_bullet_text: Travel across the 29 Schengen countries under the standard short-stay rule: 90 days in any 180-day period.

product_benefits_items.product_benefits_item_title: Access to education on the same terms as Greek nationals

product_benefits_item_bullets.product_benefits_item_bullet_text: Your children can attend Greek public schools free of charge, from primary school through public university.
Once you have completed a period of lawful residence and met the residence, language, and integration conditions set by Greek law, you may apply for naturalization.
Visa-free or eVisa access to more than 180 destinations, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Japan, and countries across Europe.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: What is a Golden Visa, and is it different from permanent residence?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: The Golden Visa is Greece's long-term residence permit for investors.

In practice it gives your family many of the same day-to-day rights as permanent residence: you can live in Greece, start a business, and send your children to school (salaried employment is not permitted).
The card is valid for 5 years and is renewable every 5 years, provided the conditions continue to be met.
It can put you on the pathway to Greek citizenship if you meet the residence, language, and integration conditions set by law.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: Does the Golden Visa allow free movement in the Schengen Area and the EU?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: Short stays in the Schengen Area — not a right to live or work elsewhere in the EU
The Golden Visa allows travel within the Schengen Area under the short-stay rules of 90 days in any 180-day period.
Travel to EU countries outside the Schengen Area still requires a visitor visa under each country's rules.
The right to live, work, and study in any EU country arises only once you hold Greek citizenship.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: What is the difference between Schengen and the EU?

product_faq_item_sections.product_faq_item_section_heading: Schengen is not the same as the EU

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: The EU — the European Union: an intergovernmental organization of 27 countries.
Schengen: an area of free movement between its member countries.
Some EU countries are not in Schengen, and the reverse is also true.
Greece is a member of both the Schengen Area and the EU.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: Can my children study free of charge?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: Free of charge at Greek public institutions.
From primary school through postgraduate study.

Investment funds from an unlawful source, which leads to refusal.

product_faq_item_sections.product_faq_item_section_note: Every family documents this differently — contact IMM Group for advice on your own situation.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: How long is the Golden Visa valid, and how is it renewed?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: A 5-year card, renewable every 5 years
You still own the property
A clean criminal record (police clearance certificate)
After 7 years: you may apply for Greek citizenship if you meet the residence and language conditions.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: How are dependents' cards renewed?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: Main applicant and spouse: renewals on the same terms, with no limit on the number of renewals, as long as you still own the property and your criminal records remain clean.
Dependent children: renewals are available only until age 24

product_faq_item_sections.product_faq_item_section_heading: There are 3 options once a child turns 24:

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: Your child applies for Greek citizenship, if eligible, to keep the right of residence.
You name a child under 18 as the main applicant under the new rules.
You transfer the property to your child so that they can keep renewing, though this takes more time and costs more.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: How many days a year must I spend in Greece?

product_faq_item_sections.product_faq_item_section_heading: No minimum stay is required to keep the Golden Visa.

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: You do not need to live in Greece to hold and renew your Golden Visa.
If you plan to apply for Greek citizenship later, you will need to meet the residence and integration conditions set by Greek law.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: What are the requirements for Greek citizenship?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: Actual residence in Greece for 7 full years — at least 183 days each year
A source of income in Greece
Greek language at B1 level, plus passing the citizenship exam on history, culture, and institutions
Evidence of integration into Greek society
No criminal record in Greece or abroad
Schooling in Greece for 9 years (primary and secondary), or
Schooling in Greece for 6 years (secondary) before age 18

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: What does Greek citizenship give you?

product_faq_item_section_bullets.product_faq_item_section_bullet_text: Full EU citizenship rights.
Freedom to live, work, and study in any EU country.

product_faq_items.product_faq_item_question: Is there an age limit for applicants?
